newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Scottish Hydro eyes div growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Scottish Hydro eyes div growth.

text.p: Electricity generator Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc aims to continue delivering dividend growth through expanding its business, chief executive Roger Young said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
"We aim to keep on delivering dividend improvement..., doing it by expanding the business," he said.
Scottish Hydro raised its interim dividend 11.2 percent to 5.28 pence per share while half-year pre-tax profits edged down to 61.3 million stg from 61.7 million stg previously.

The company, which gains much of its capacity from hydro-electric generation, should improve its share of the electricity market to seven percent by 1999 from current levels of around four percent, Young added.

He said the company's plans to take control of Keadby power station by buying out its 50 percent partner, United Utilities, should "increase costs but also increase profits," adding an extra 340 megaWatts of generation capacity to the portfolio.

Scottish Power said in a statement with half-year results that it was the preferred bidder for United Utilities' stake and the deal should be completed by the end of the financial year, increasing gearing to around 50 percent.
Young said that talks with British Gas on the sale of its domestic gas supply business in England and Scotland had broken down for administrative rather than commercial reasons.
"There was no serious commercial difficulty that caused the project to be dropped...British Gas had a lot of competition for its (administrative) resources," he said.
British Gas and Scottish Hydro announced the talks had been called off in September after newspaper reports suggested a sale might be in the offing for 250 million stg.
Young said he was not optimistic any discussions would resume, however, as "deals tend to have their day".
He said there were other discussions "around, but nothing that we can talk about."
